description: Whether the BS PxWeb instance exposes the standard PxWeb JSON/REST API (typically an /api/v1/ path) was not established in this pass; only the HTML tablelist views were observed.
No RSS/Atom feed or email-alert endpoint was confirmed for /sl/mediji/objave or the publications index, so new-release detection currently depends on polling plus the release-calendar JSON.

The PxWeb payment folder contains a live table set and a parallel archive set with entirely different ids (T_2_8_*, T_2_9_*, T_2_10_*, T_2_11_*, T_2_12_*), reflecting the ECB/2020/59 reporting change in force from 1 January 2022. The concordance between old and new series was not obtained.

Payment fraud statistics (reported under EBA/GL/2018/05 as amended, and folded into the main payment-statistics return from 2022) were confirmed to be collected by BS, but no published SI fraud statistics output was located within this cell.

BS sources repeatedly point to commercial infrastructure actors (notably Bankart d.o.o. as the domestic card/ATM processor, and licensed e-money institutions such as Petrol Pay and Paywiser) but publish no operational data about them.

English mirrors exist for the statistics domain pages and the PxWeb warehouse, but oversight, reporting-instruction and register pages were found predominantly in Slovenian; English equivalents were not verified for those.
Exact SDMX dataflow and series-key patterns for Slovenia in PSS, PTT, PCP and BKN were not resolved (only dataset landing pages).
ECB oversight/infrastructure sources (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement usage, card scheme oversight, SEPA reachability via EPC) and ECB digital-euro progress reports were not covered in this pass.
EU open-data catalogue (data.europa.eu) was not searched directly as an aggregator index for SI payments/banking datasets.
Slovenian-language coverage in this cell is structurally thin because supranational aggregators publish in English; only NCB relays provided sl terms.
Break in series caused by the shift to ECB Regulation ECB/2020/59 (payments statistics from 2022 reference periods) was not characterised.

Discretionary and non-grocery merchant verticals were not covered in this pass: DIY/technical (Merkur, Bauhaus, Obi), drogerija (dm, Müller), fashion, and the hospitality/HoReCa till estate (SKD 56.x), which is a very large slice of fiscally verified invoices.

Acquirer-side merchant counts (number of merchant contracts, terminals per acquirer) for Slovenia were not located in public form; Bankart's role is described qualitatively but per-acquirer merchant/terminal splits were not found.

The FURS open-data resources sighted are per-year files; it is not established from this pass how far back the series runs, how quickly the current year is refreshed, or whether historic files are revised.
Italian- and Hungarian-language merchant sources for the bilingual border municipalities (Obalno-kraška, Prekmurje) were not searched, and no cross-border-shopping merchant angle was covered.

The live Slovenian policy debate on mandatory cash acceptance and on obligatory card acceptance by merchants (referenced in Forbes SI reporting on Ministry of Finance proposals) was only touched at the edge; primary Ministry of Finance / draft-legislation sources were not pulled.
Card-issuing/personalisation and HSM/security vendors serving SI banks are entirely unmapped (Cetis, Idemia, Thales, G+D, Utimaco).
Vendor LinkedIn pages — where SI go-lives are announced earliest — are not collectable with the current toolchain.
Cash-cycle vendors (cash-in-transit, cash recyclers, branch automation) touching Slovenian cash-usage data were not searched at all.

Vendor-side material in SI is heavily English even when the vendor is domestic; several Slovenian-language queries returned regulator or media pages rather than vendor reference pages, so local-language vendor vocabulary is still under-tested.
Smaller SI software houses plausibly serving banks (Marand, Unistar LC, Genis, Mikrocop, Nova Vizija, In516ht, Trigal) were not individually checked for bank references.
Vendor references found are point-in-time; no archived-snapshot strategy is defined, so silently removed customer logos (a churn signal) would be missed.
No Slovene-language podcast, newsletter or video-commentary source was identified for banking and payments, though such formats increasingly carry off-record executive commentary.
No historical media archive route was established for reconstructing fee or ATM-network changes before roughly 2015; paywalled dailies do not expose deep archives publicly.

English-language commentary specifically on the Slovenian payments market is thin and mostly from non-Slovene vendors (The Fintech Times, GlobalData, TheBanks.eu, sloveniabusiness.eu), which lag and simplify the Slovene reporting.
Merchant- and acquirer-side media commentary (retail trade press, hospitality associations complaining about POS acceptance costs) was not covered by this cell's searches.
All URLs in this slice are search-derived; none were fetched and none should be treated as liveness-verified.

The only genuinely SI-specific instrument-level market sizing (GlobalData, ResearchAndMarkets yearbook, Argus Advisory) is entirely behind commercial paywalls; only abstracts and press releases are harvestable.

Nothing in this cell produced independent ATM/POS terminal-estimate series or cash-logistics analysis; the aggregators reference POS/ATM counts only inside paywalled products, and no consultancy paper on SI cash infrastructure was found.

Slovenian-language consultancy output is thin: apart from Deloitte SI's DBM article and EY SI's insights feed, the Big Four publish about Slovenia mainly in English regional reports. Local-language depth comes instead from academia (RUL, CEK) and survey/media relays.

Global research houses likely to hold SI cuts were not individually confirmed this pass: Capgemini World Payments Report, Roland Berger, Oliver Wyman, Kearney European Retail Banking Radar, and Euromonitor/Mintel consumer-finance data.
Slovenian survey houses beyond Valicon (Mediana, Ninamedia, Aragon, Parsifal) were not individually searched, and none was confirmed to run a payments-specific tracker.

EU-level adjudication touching Slovenia (European Commission competition decisions, CJEU/Curia rulings on interchange and payment accounts, EBA consumer-trends and payment-fraud reports) was not systematically covered in this cell.

No verification pass was made on AVK's decision-archive pagination depth or on whether older interchange/banking cases sit only in the pre-2013 Urad za varstvo konkurence (UVK) archive under a different domain or naming.
Complaint and dispute data specific to ATM/POS access and card acceptance (as opposed to accounts and credit) is thin; no source found that breaks complaints down by card/ATM/POS category.

Second-tier consumer bodies were not explored: Mednarodni inštitut za potrošniške raziskave (MIPOR, ZPS research arm), Zveza potrošnikov' European Consumer Centre Slovenia (ECC-Net SI), and the Ministry of Economy consumer-protection directorate.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live; all entries rest on search-result evidence only.

Commercial-bank careers pages are covered only for Deželna banka and (indirectly) NLB. NLB, OTP banka (ex Nova KBM), Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, SKB (OTP Group), Addiko, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica and Sparkasse careers pages and their LinkedIn hiring feeds were not reached.

Cash-usage weak signals (CIT companies, cash-in-transit and ATM-estate operators, independent ATM deployers, Bankart's ATM outsourcing partners) were not searched at all. Job ads and tenders from CIT/ATM service firms are the clearest early indicator of ATM estate contraction or expansion.

Public procurement / tender portals (e-JN, portal javnih narocil) were not covered in this cell. Bank and public-sector tenders for POS terminals, ATM servicing and payment software are a strong pre-announcement signal, and award notices disclose volumes and values.

English-language coverage in this slice is thin — only one en query completed successfully (the awards query) plus the BSI Fintech Hub en page. The en-language regional event circuit (payments conferences in AT/HR/RS with Slovenian speakers) is unexplored.

No systematic snapshot inventory was built. The Wayback CDX API was identified as the method but not executed, so it is unknown which SI payment-statistics pages are already well-archived and which are at risk of loss.
This cell supplies denominators only. Actual payment, card, ATM and POS transaction counts for Slovenia are published by Banka Slovenije and the ECB, which fall outside this cell.
Eurostat re-publishes the Slovenian ICT household/enterprise survey, HBS and national accounts in harmonised form with a stable bulk-download API, which was not explored in this pass.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live by this agent; all URLs come from search-result evidence and cross-references between sources.

SURS retail turnover and ICT indicators are national and, at best, cohesion-region level; no municipality-level or merchant-category-level breakdown suitable for terminal-density modelling was identified.
The household budget survey (APG) runs only every few years while payment statistics are monthly or quarterly, and the COICOP 1999 to COICOP 2018 switch introduces a break in the consumption series.
No SKD/NACE activity-code sweep was performed to build the candidate list of Slovenian ATM servicing, POS terminal supply and payment-technology companies from the business register.

Card acquiring in Slovenia is largely performed by banks and by the domestic processor, so no acquirer-specific list was located; scheme-side sources (Visa/Mastercard licensed acquirer and principal-member lists for SI) were not searched in this slice.
The exact machine-readable interfaces for AJPES (ePRS reuse service, OPSI resource endpoints) and for EBA EUCLID were not read in detail; only their existence and general terms were established.

JOLP is described as giving access to recent years online, with older years obtainable only at AJPES offices; the precise online retention window was not confirmed, and eObjave documents are retained online for only one year.
Slovenian-language coverage was strong for AJPES and Banka Slovenije, but no Slovenian-language terms were available or used for the supranational EBA/EUCLID sources, which are English-only.

State-owned / public-interest entities that plausibly tender ATM, POS, cash-handling or core-banking services were not individually investigated: Pošta Slovenije (postal counters and cash), SID banka, SDH (Slovenski državni holding), UJP (Uprava RS za javna plačila), DARS (tolling POS/payment acceptance), Slovenske železnice, and large municipalities.
No verified CPV code set for ATM/cash dispensers, card issuing/personalisation, and core banking software.

Local-language glossary is solid for cash transport and ATMs but thin for card issuing/personalisation and core banking. Terms such as 'personalizacija plačilnih kartic', 'izdajanje kartic', 'jedrni bančni sistem', 'core banking sistem', 'kartično poslovanje' were used only partially; noisy terms identified: 'bankomati' (dominated by bank ATM-locator pages), 'razpis' (also means scholarship/donation calls), 'javni razpis' (grants, not procurement).
Slovenian national open data starts at 2013 (Evidenca javnih naročil); pre-2013 national coverage was not established, though TED FTP reportedly reaches back to 1993.
Automated access characteristics (robots.txt, rate limits, JS-rendering, ToS) were not tested for enarocanje.si, ejn.gov.si, erar.si or dkom.si.

All URLs in this slice come from search-result metadata; none were fetched and confirmed reachable in this pass, and several deep PDF paths (year-foldered NLB, ISP, OTP downloadfile ids) are of the kind that rotate.

Bank sustainability/ESG reports, Pillar 3 disclosures beyond Gorenjska banka and Sparkasse, and AJPES JOLP (public filed annual accounts) were not systematically searched, though AJPES is the statutory repository where every Slovenian bank files.

Foreign-bank branches and niche private issuers in Slovenia (e.g. BKS Bank AG branch, N Banka wind-down legacy, Deželna banka Slovenije, UniCredit Banka Slovenija) were not covered in this pass; DBS and UniCredit in particular are material card/ATM issuers.
Branch/ATM locator pages were classified as indirect sources on reasoning, but their backing data endpoints, robots.txt posture and record counts were not inspected.

The cell rationale assumes private banks bypass public procurement portals, but bank-to-vendor relationships for ATM hardware, card personalisation and processing (e.g. Bankart as the shared national processor) are not visible in the sources gathered here.

National Payments Council minutes (38 sessions, 2014–2026) and the 'Strategija razvoja plačilnega trga v Sloveniji 2024–2028' were identified but not read in this pass; only one minutes PDF URL was captured.
Bančni vestnik full texts (1952–2026) are partly login-gated; the free subset was not enumerated.
TZS member area and its T-Informacije bulletin, and OZS member advisories, are unindexed.
Združenje Povezani smo was identified only through media coverage; its own website/domain was not located, so its primary materials (petition text, submissions) are uncaptured.
ZBS's memberships in supranational bodies (e.g. European Banking Federation, ESBG/WSBI, EPC) were not confirmed in this pass.
Slovensko zavarovalno združenje (Slovenian Insurance Association) is an NSP member but was not profiled; likewise the e-commerce/online-retail association layer was not searched.

English-language association output was thin: only ZBS (EN annual reports, EN site, Bančni vestnik English special issues) and TZS (/en landing) offered EN material; GZS PTZ, OZS, ZPS and the NSP minutes are effectively Slovenian-only.
Per-acquirer tariff/price lists ('cenik', 'tarifa') of SI banks acting as acquirers (NLB, OTP, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Deželna banka, SKB/OTP) were not individually located in this pass.
Bankart's recent annual reports and any published statistics/newsroom feed were not enumerated from the site itself (only via search).
Visa's Slovenian-language presence (visa.si / visa.com sl-si) was not checked for SI-specific interchange or press pages.
Independent ATM operators / white-label ATM deployers and cash-in-transit players in SI (relevant to cash usage and ATM data) were not covered in this cell's pass.
Slovenian Competition Protection Agency (AVK) and EU Commission antitrust files on card interchange were not searched.
All URLs in this slice were obtained from search results or a single fetch and are unverified for liveness by design.

The Banka Slovenije register of licensed payment institutions, e-money institutions and account information service providers, and the EBA central credit-institution/payment-institution register, were referenced in secondary sources but not directly located and pinned to a URL in this pass.

Domestic acquiring/POS and A2A-adjacent actors were not searched in this pass: Halcom (corporate e-banking and payment software), Petrol Pay / Petrol's QR ecosystem, Nexi/Worldline activity in SI, Rekono (identity provider used for wallet onboarding), and small-bank Flik participants such as Delavska hranilnica and Gorenjska banka.

The ECB SPACE study (Study on the Payment Attitudes of Consumers in the Euro area) and any Banka Slovenije consumer payment-habits survey were not searched, yet these are the canonical bridge between instant/wallet adoption and cash usage at point of sale.

SURS (Statistični urad RS) and its SiStat database were not queried for ICT/e-commerce usage indicators (share of individuals using mobile payments, internet banking penetration), which provide independent adoption denominators.

Public procurement portals (e-JN / Portal javnih naročil) and Diavgeia-equivalent transparency channels were not searched. Tenders for instant-payment, wallet or e-invoicing infrastructure reveal spend, vendors and roadmap ahead of any press release.

Several candidate URLs were assembled from actor knowledge rather than confirmed in a search result: the EPC SCT Inst register export path, the Wero/EPI domains, the ZBS Bančni vestnik e-archive root, the Valú product page and the AJPES eRacuni deep link.
Commercial market reports (GlobalData 'Slovenia Cards and Payments to 2028', Statista card-purchase series) surfaced but were not assessed for licensing or value.
Cash recycling and automated cash deposit infrastructure in Slovenia is entirely uncovered - no terminology, vendors, bank deployments or central bank accreditation lists were identified.
ATM withdrawal volumes and values, and any geographic breakdown of cash withdrawal activity, were not located in national sources.
ATM hardware, software and managed-services vendors serving the Slovenian estate were not investigated at all in this pass - only deployers, banks and CIT firms were mapped.
Public procurement records were identified as the likely richest untapped source for both municipal ATM subsidies and bank ATM/CIT contracts, but were not searched in this pass.
The individual written responses to the ZDUPS public consultation (closed 17 August 2026) were not retrieved - only third-party reporting on ZBS's and OZS's positions.

Only one subsidising municipality (Logatec) was identified by name; the population of Slovenian municipalities that subsidise or tender for ATMs is unknown, and there is no consolidated register of ATM closure events at settlement level.
